panSubstrates.name: Rough Sand-Cast Iron (e.g., Traditional Lodge)
panSubstrates.patinaAdhesionStrength: High (mechanical interlocking into microscopic surface pores)
panSubstrates.acidVulnerabilityRate: Moderate (thick initial patina resists brief contact, but acid penetrates deep pores)
panSubstrates.description: Manufactured using sand mold casting, resulting in a microscopic pebble-grain texture. The high graphite flake content and micro-crevices provide substantial mechanical keying for polymerized drying oils. While a mature multi-layer patina resists brief acidic deglazing, prolonged acid contact penetrates porous grain boundaries, attacking bare iron beneath.

panSubstrates.name: Machined / Polished Smooth Cast Iron (Vintage & Artisan)
panSubstrates.matrixType: Fine Grain Grey Iron (CNC Milled Surface)
panSubstrates.patinaAdhesionStrength: Moderate (reduced mechanical keying; relies more on chemical covalent bonding)
panSubstrates.acidVulnerabilityRate: High initially; moderate once deep micro-polymerized crosslinking is established
panSubstrates.description: Smooth CNC-milled or hand-polished cooking surface resembling vintage Griswold or Wagner skillets. Without sand-cast micro-cavities, the initial seasoning layer is thinner and more vulnerable to shearing and acid-induced delamination, but releases food exceptionally well.

panSubstrates.name: Thin-Gauge Carbon Steel (1.5mm–2.0mm Crepe / Omelette Pan)
panSubstrates.patinaAdhesionStrength: Low-to-Moderate (ultra-smooth surface lacks micro-cavities; prone to sheet flaking)
panSubstrates.acidVulnerabilityRate: Very High (rapid acid-catalyzed stripping; fast temperature swings accelerate spalling)
panSubstrates.description: Lightweight, stamped cold-rolled carbon steel favored for French omelette and crepe pans. Rapid thermal response causes localized thermal expansion gradients. Acidic deglazing agents (white wine, lemon juice) rapidly dissolve the thin metal-oxide bonding interface, causing the seasoning to peel off in visible black flecks.

panSubstrates.name: Heavy-Gauge Restaurant Carbon Steel (3.0mm–3.5mm Skillet / Wok)
panSubstrates.patinaAdhesionStrength: Moderate (superior thermal inertia stabilizes seasoning under commercial heat)
panSubstrates.acidVulnerabilityRate: Moderate-High (withstands rapid 60-second pan sauce deglaze, but strips during braising)
panSubstrates.description: Thick, heavy commercial carbon steel pan combining the responsiveness of steel with the thermal mass of cast iron. Widely used in professional restaurant lines. Able to withstand rapid flash-deglazing with wine if immediately scraped and washed, but will suffer severe patina etching if acidic sauces simmer longer than 5 minutes.

panSubstrates.name: Enameled Cast Iron (Vitreous Porcelain Enamel Control)
panSubstrates.patinaAdhesionStrength: N/A (Non-reactive glass coating; requires zero seasoning)
panSubstrates.description: Heavy cast iron core hermetically sealed beneath multiple coats of inorganic vitreous porcelain enamel fired at 800°C (1472°F). Completely impervious to acidic foods, prolonged tomato simmers, and wine reductions. Zero iron leaching, zero metallic taste, and zero seasoning required.

panSubstrates.name: Marine-Grade 316 Stainless Steel (Acid-Proof Metal Control)
panSubstrates.acidVulnerabilityRate: Extremely Low (immune to food acids; molybdenum prevents pitting corrosion)
panSubstrates.description: High-performance cookware alloy with 16–18% chromium, 10–12% nickel, and 2–3% molybdenum. The self-healing passive chromium(III) oxide film resists boiling acetic, citric, and malic acids without seasoning or degradation.

foodMatrices.name: Slow-Simmered Tomato Marinara / Bolognese
foodMatrices.discolorationRisk: Severe (Iron reacts with tomato lycopene and polyphenols, turning sauce dark muddy brown)
foodMatrices.description: Classic kitchen safety hazard. The continuous simmering action of aqueous citric acid (pH 3.8) at 90°C hydrolyzes ester crosslinks in polymerized oil layers, dissolving elemental iron and converting it to soluble ferrous citrate.

foodMatrices.name: Red Wine Pan Deglaze & Reduction (Bordelaise / Au Jus)
foodMatrices.category: High Acid, Alcohol Solvent & High Heat
foodMatrices.discolorationRisk: Extreme (Red wine anthocyanins and tannins chelate iron, precipitating inky black iron-tannate complexes)
foodMatrices.description: A double threat: ethanol acts as an organic solvent that swells and softens the fatty acid polymer matrix, while tartaric acid aggressively chelates iron ions from bare metal. Forms astringent iron tannates that ruin wine flavor.

foodMatrices.name: Lemon Butter Piccata & White Wine Reduction
foodMatrices.discolorationRisk: High (Turns light golden lemon sauce into an unappealing murky grey emulsion)
foodMatrices.description: High concentration of free hydronium ions (pH 2.6) rapidly attacks metal grain boundaries. Even a 90-second pan deglaze strips superficial carbon steel seasoning, releasing sharp metallic ferrous ions into the sauce.

foodMatrices.name: Balsamic Vinegar & Caramelized Onion Glaze
foodMatrices.category: Volatile Acetic Acid & Sugar Carboxylic Chelation
foodMatrices.discolorationRisk: Moderate (Dark sauce masks color, but metallic penny aftertaste is intense)
foodMatrices.description: Hot acetic acid vapors actively etch exposed iron while caramelized sugars form sticky coordinate complexes with dissolved iron, ripping weakened seasoning layers right off the pan during stirring.

foodMatrices.name: Apple Cider & Pork Chop Braise
foodMatrices.discolorationRisk: High (Oxidizes cider polyphenols to muddy greyish-green hue)
foodMatrices.description: Malic acid chelation dissolves iron steadily during a 30-to-45 minute braise, resulting in significant iron migration and stripping the pan's bronze patina down to dull grey metal.

foodMatrices.name: High-Heat Ribeye Steak Sear with Tallow / Ghee
foodMatrices.description: Optimal cast iron cooking environment. Neutral pH and high heat promote further lipid crosslinking and carbonization, depositing fresh microscopic seasoning layers rather than stripping them.

patinaMaturityLevels.name: Raw / Stripped Bare Metal (0 Seasoning Layers)
patinaMaturityLevels.description: Freshly stripped or unseasoned raw metal. Direct contact between food acids and reactive iron leads to maximum possible leaching and immediate off-flavors.

patinaMaturityLevels.name: Factory Pre-Seasoned (1–2 Thin Sprayed Layers, ~3 µm)
patinaMaturityLevels.metallicTasteSensitivity: High (superficial layer etches through within 3–5 minutes of acid simmer)
patinaMaturityLevels.description: Standard commercial pre-seasoning using electrostatic oil spray baked at high speed. Provides basic rust protection during shipping and storage, but lacks the high-density crosslinking required to resist organic food acids.

patinaMaturityLevels.name: Well-Maintained Home Seasoning (4–6 Oven Layers, ~12 µm)
patinaMaturityLevels.metallicTasteSensitivity: Moderate (withstands brief 2–3 minute wine deglazing; degrades during prolonged simmering)
patinaMaturityLevels.description: Formed through multiple cycles of ultra-thin drying oil application (e.g., grapeseed or flaxseed) baked past the smoke point. Offers substantial barrier protection against brief flash deglazing.

patinaMaturityLevels.name: Heirloom Multi-Year Patina (15+ Crosslinked Layers, ~28 µm)
patinaMaturityLevels.metallicTasteSensitivity: Low (dense polymer network buffers acid contact, preserving taste during quick sauces)
patinaMaturityLevels.description: Decades of regular cooking with unsaturated fats creating a rock-hard, glassy, dense crosslinked carbon-polymer hybrid matrix. Substantially suppresses iron migration during short acidic pan sauces.

healthProfiles.name: Healthy Adult Male (Age 19–50)
healthProfiles.clinicalRisk: Low; iron leached is easily managed unless daily intake chronically exceeds 45 mg.
healthProfiles.description: Adult males possess lower baseline iron requirements (8 mg/day) and can absorb iron without issue up to the UL threshold of 45 mg/day.

healthProfiles.name: Premenopausal Adult Female (Age 19–50)
healthProfiles.clinicalRisk: Beneficial in moderation for iron-deficient diets; still vulnerable to metallic off-flavors.
healthProfiles.description: Higher monthly physiological iron losses increase RDA to 18 mg/day. Mild iron leaching from cooking can help meet daily intake, but heavy acidic reductions still cause digestive irritation and metallic food taste.

healthProfiles.name: Toddler / Young Child (15 kg body weight)
healthProfiles.clinicalRisk: High vulnerability to acute iron gastrointestinal toxicity (corrosive gut mucosal damage at >20 mg/kg).
healthProfiles.description: Children under 6 have lower blood volume and immature iron-binding capacity. Ingestion of acidic tomato sauce heavily cooked in stripped cast iron (yielding 30–50 mg Fe) can induce nausea, vomiting, and mucosal ulceration.

healthProfiles.name: Hereditary Hemochromatosis Carrier / Iron Overload Risk
healthProfiles.clinicalRisk: Contraindicated: Uncontrolled intestinal iron absorption causes hepatic and myocardial siderosis.
healthProfiles.description: Affects ~1 in 200 individuals of Northern European descent (HFE C282Y/H63D gene mutations). The body lacks a mechanism to excrete excess iron. Cooking acidic meals in reactive bare cast iron or carbon steel should be strictly avoided in favor of enameled cookware.

scientificReferences.title: Iron content of food cooked in iron utensils
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Simmering acidic applesauce in a cast iron skillet increased iron concentration from 0.35 mg/100g to 7.38 mg/100g (over 20-fold increase). Spaghetti sauce iron spiked from 0.61 mg to 5.77 mg/100g.

scientificReferences.title: Iron content of Massachusetts school lunches cooked in cast iron vs non-stick cookware
scientificReferences.journal: Journal of the American Dietetic Association
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Acidic tomato-based dishes cooked in unenameled iron cookware increased total iron content by up to 845%, providing significant supplemental iron while noticeably darkening red sauces.

scientificReferences.authors: Sharma S, Kulkarni R, Kulkarni V.
scientificReferences.title: Effect of cooking in iron pots on iron content and organoleptic properties of foods
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Iron-tannate and iron-polyphenol complexes formed in wine and vegetable reductions created astringent sensory rejection when soluble iron exceeded 5 mg per 250g serving.

scientificReferences.authors: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA NDA Panel).
scientificReferences.title: Scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level for iron
scientificReferences.keyFinding: Confirmed 45 mg/day as the adult Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL) to avoid systemic gastrointestinal mucosal irritation and hepatocellular oxidative stress.
